Protective: Supportive partner; proactive help-seeking; reassurance from clinician

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Health-related anxiety
- Patient Goal(s): Gain reassurance; reduce panic and catastrophic thoughts about current symptoms
- Clinical Goal(s): Decrease anxiety severity; enhance coping while awaiting ENT/neurological assessment
- Actions (Patient):
  • Limit unstructured internet searches about symptoms  
  • Practice relaxation/breathing techniques daily (education to be provided)  
  • Attend scheduled face-to-face GP/clinic appointment today for physical assessment
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Provide brief psycho-education on health anxiety and normalise worry  
  • Offer printed/online vetted resources on managing health-related worry  
  • Consider short CBT-based self-help materials or referral to primary care mental health service (IAPT/CBT) if anxiety persists after physical evaluation  
  • Reassess anxiety symptoms at next visit

Secondary Problem: Functional/occupational impact
- Patient Goal(s): Return to usual training schedule without excessive worry
- Clinical Goal(s): Support graded return to activity once medical clearance obtained; monitor stress levels
- Actions (Patient): Follow medical recommendations; communicate with employer/trainer regarding temporary adjustments
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Coordinate with ENT/neurology for timely diagnostics; provide medical certification if work restrictions needed

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of health anxiety, role of reassurance, relaxation strategies, when to seek urgent help
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalating worry, insomnia, avoidance of activities, persistent checking behaviours
- Coping Strategies: Scheduled worry time, mindfulness breathing, engaging in daily routine, seeking support from partner or GP

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (verbal)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not yet (to be provided after face-to-face assessment)
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently

- Review Date: To be set at post-clinic follow-up (recommended within 4 weeks)
